image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a ground covered with dry leaves and dirt. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, grey/brown body plumage, and orange webbed feet. It is viewed from a high-angle side profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a distinct yellow-green coloration typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible against the dark green head feathers and appears black/dark brown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and oval, consistent with a waterfowl. The feather texture appears dense and layered.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: glossy green head, distinct white collar, and mixed grey/brown body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg and foot are clearly visible. The foot shows the characteristic palmate structure with webbing between the forward-facing toes.
The folded wing is visible along the side of the body, showing proper layering of flight feathers and speculum (blue/purple patch).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central rectrices (drake feathers) is visible at the rear of the bird.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or misclassified bird types.
To verify the structural integrity of the legs and feet, ensuring no fusion or extra limbs, despite the 'limbless' note in instructions, ducks have distinct limbs requiring pose validation.
To closely inspect the webbing and toe separation for any melting or boundary errors common in AI generation of complex foot structures.
To detect subtle texture anomalies, smearing, or inconsistent lighting in the feathers and background leaves.

focus_areas: Webbed foot structure and toe separation
Feather texture consistency and edge sharpness
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the webbed feet; AI often struggles with the specific geometry of palmate feet. Verify that the blue speculum patch on the wing is structurally integrated into the wing feathers and not just painted on. Check for any 'haloing' around the green head where it meets the background.
